sections.title: Planning with Shelf Life
sections.text:
8.1 Planning with Shelf Life
One of the advanced features in PP/DS that no other planning tool in any SAP system
offers is shelf-life planning. Planning with shelf life is a very critical requirement for
industries such as food, beverage, and pharma/life sciences.
Embedded PP/DS can consider the shelf-life date while planning and creating procure-
ment proposals and in dynamic pegging. A receipt element in PP/DS that will expire on
a certain date won’t be considered for fulfilling a requirement element that is after the
expiry date. In addition, if the minimum required shelf life is defined, the receipt ele-
ment should have the defined minimum shelf life remaining to be considered for peg-
ging to a requirement element.
The following PP/DS applications consider shelf life:
 Heuristics
The planning of standard lots heuristic (Transaction /SAPAPO/HEU_PLAN_STAN-
DARDLOTS) considers the shelf-life data defined while planning. The shelf-life data
restrictions can be violated if capacity or scheduling constraints are violated during
the planning. But the Alert Monitor (discussed in Chapter 7) can be configured to
raise an alert when the shelf-life conditions are violated.
 Pegging
If shelf-life data is maintained in the product master, dynamic pegging will always
consider this data while creating the pegging between the receipt and requirement
elements.

8 Advanced PP/DS Features
472
 PP/DS optimizer
The PP/DS optimizer considers the pegging relationship between the receipt and
requirement elements that are created based on shelf life.
 Detailed scheduling
The detailed scheduling strategies consider the shelf-life data in rescheduling activities
and operations in order not to violate the dynamic pegging created between the receipt
and requirement elements, which is created considering the shelf-life restrictions.
The steps to set up the shelf-life planning scenario in PP/DS are covered in the follow-
ing sections.

sections.title: Master Data
sections.text:
8.1.1 Master Data
The master data for shelf-life planning is maintained in the material master for the SAP
S/4HANA system. The required material-specific data is maintained in Transaction
MM02 by navigating to the Advanced Planning view and the Plant data / stor. 1 view
(see Figure 8.1) of the material master.
Batches are commonly used to hold the shelf-life characteristics of the materials in SAP
S/4HANA, and the same are transferred to embedded PP/DS along with the inventory
data. The SAP S/4HANA applications, such as batch management, batch determination,
and inventory management, use the shelf-life data defined in the Plant data / stor. 1
view of the material master. The data defined here for the material is global for PP/DS
and is location independent.
Figure 8.1 Defining Shelf-Life Data in the Material Master
© 

473
8.1 Planning with Shelf Life
In the Plant data / stor. 1 view under the Shelf life data section, you define the following
data:
 Min. Rem. Shelf Life
This is the minimum shelf life required for the product. In PP/DS, this value is con-
sidered during planning. When a receipt element doesn’t have the minimum shelf
life defined here, it can’t be used to fulfill a receipt element.
 Total shelf life
This is the value of the shelf life of the product. The expiry date of the receipt ele-
ment is calculated by adding the total shelf-life duration to the date it’s produced.
 Expiration Date
Here you define how the shelf-life expiry is interpreted. E signifies the expiry date
(date after which the product can’t be used), and B signifies the best before date (date
after which the product may not be usable).
Under the Shelf life data – Advanced Planning section in the Plant data / stor. 1 view of
the material master, you define the following values:
 Maturation Time
This is the time required for the product to mature before it can be used or can be
shipped out to a customer.
 Req.Max.Sh.Life
The required maximum shelf life is the maximum allowed shelf life for a product
that can be used for a requirement on the requirement date.
The values defined here for a material that is relevant for advanced planning is made
available to PP/DS immediately. When the total shelf life of a material is defined as
more than zero, the material gets enabled for shelf-life planning in PP/DS.
The activation of the shelf-life planning and the values defined in the material master
can be verified from the product master data in embedded PP/DS. As shown in Figure
8.2, from Transaction /SAPAPO/MAT1, under the Properties tab, the Shelf Life options
relevant to PP/DS are displayed. This information can only be displayed from the PP/DS
product master data, and the maintenance is done only from the SAP S/4HANA mate-
rial master. These values are location independent.
It’s also possible to maintain certain PP/DS location-specific shelf-life data in the
Advanced Planning view of the material master. If location-specific shelf-life data is
maintained in the material master, the same will be considered for planning. In the
Advanced Planning view of the material master (Transaction MM02) under the Loca-
tion Dependent Shelf-Life area, you can select the Shelf Life (Loc) checkbox, and then
define the total shelf life (Loc. Shelf Life), maturation time (Loc. Matur.Time), and Min.
Shelf Life/Max. Shelf Life options, as shown in Figure 8.3.

8 Advanced PP/DS Features
474
Figure 8.2 Shelf-Life Data in the PP/DS Product Master
Figure 8.3 Location-Dependent PP/DS Shelf-Life Data in the Material Master

sections.title: Integration of Batches with Shelf Life
sections.text:
8.1.2 Integration of Batches with Shelf Life
In planning with shelf life, it’s important to integrate the inventory data with the shelf-
life information into PP/DS, so that they can be considered during planning. Specific
prerequisites and steps are required to integrate the batches with classification (023
batch class) to PP/DS.
© 

475
8.1 Planning with Shelf Life
The advanced planning system’s (PP/DS) configuration schema should be set to
characteristics-dependent planning (CDP). The advanced planning configuration
schema can be set or verified from Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced
Planning  Basic Settings  Define Configuration Schema (CDP or Variant Configuration).
In SAP S/4HANA, when activating batch management, the batch level should be main-
tained at the material level so that the batch class type 023 can be assigned to the
batches. The integration of batches with classification to PP/DS is only possible with
the 023 class type. The batch level of SAP S/4HANA batch management can be set or
verified from Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Logistics – General  Batch Man-
agement  Specify Batch Level and Activate Status Management, as shown in Figure 8.4.
Select the Batch unique at material level option, and click the Save button.
Figure 8.4 Batch Management at the Material Level: Customizing
The creation of the batch class (class type 023) should follow these specifics to integrate
with the shelf-life data in embedded PP/DS (refer to Chapter 2, Section 2.6, for details):
1. Create an organization area for the classification data to be used in creating the inte-
gration model and integrating the class to PP/DS.
2. Create a class of type 023 using Transaction CL02, and assign the organizational unit
and the following characteristics in the Char. tab of the transaction (bottom part of
Figure 8.5):
– LOBM_APO_SL_MAX (Max Shelf-Life/Shlf-Lfe in Sec)
– LOBM_APO_SL_MIN (Min Shelf-Life/Maturity in Sec)
– LOBM_APO_SL_UTC (Reference Time Stamp of Batch)
– LOBM_VERAB (Availability Date)
– LOBM_VFDAT (Expiration Date, Shelf Life)
– LOBM_HSDAT (Date when Batch Was Produced)
Assignment of the LOBM_APO_SL_MAX, LOBM_APO_SL_MIN, and LOBM_APO_SL_
UTC characteristics is mandatory because the mapping of the characteristics’ values
to PP/DS checks for these characteristics’ names specifically. Without using these
characteristics, the shelf-life data of the batches aren’t integrated to PP/DS.

8 Advanced PP/DS Features
476
3. In the Basic data tab, assign the organizational area to the class in the Organizational
area field.
4. In the Char. tab for the characteristics containing the characters SL, assign the orga-
nizational area in the Org. Areas column, as shown in Figure 8.5.
Figure 8.5 Prerequisite for Class and Characteristics
5. In SAP S/4HANA, only the LOBM_VERAB (Availability Date), LOBM_VFDAT (Expira-
tion Date, Shelf Life), and LOBM_HSDAT (Date when Batch Was Produced) are calcu-
lated during the SAP S/4HANA material movement transactions, such as goods
receipt (GR) postings. But the shelf-life characteristics are calculated in the back-
ground by the object dependencies assigned to these characteristics.
In the standard SAP S/4HANA system, program RVBCOR08 is delivered to generate
the object dependencies for these characteristics. Execute the report once in the sys-
tem from Transaction SE38 or Transaction SA38.
6. After the program is executed, check the object dependencies to make sure they are
created with the Released status. Go to the class, double-click on the characteristics,
© 

477
8.1 Planning with Shelf Life
and choose More  Extras  Object Dependencies  Assignments, or click on the Object
Dependencies button (the zig-zagging arrows) on the screen, as shown in Figure 8.6.
7. Check the status of the object dependency shown in Figure 8.6 by checking the value
in the S column. In this example, the status is 1, which means Released.
The object dependencies are assigned to the characteristics LOBM_VERAB, LOBM_
VFDAT, and LOBM_HSDAT, which are used by the system to calculate the values for
the other three characteristics, LOBM_APO_SL_MIN, LOBM_APO_SL_MAX, and
LOBM_APO_SL_UTC, respectively.
Figure 8.6 Object Dependencies for Characteristics Relevant to Shelf Life
Tip
If the object dependencies aren’t assigned to the characteristics, execute program RVB-
COR08. The execution of this report will generate the object dependencies that can be
verified from the characteristics (refer to Figure 8.6).

8 Advanced PP/DS Features
478
8. Create an integration model for the organizational area assigned to the class, and
activate the integration model (see Chapter 2, Section 2.1). This will create class type
230 for use in PP/DS. You can verify that the class with class type 230 was created
with the same class name in Transaction CL02.
9. Activate batch management for the material from Transaction MM02, navigate to
the Plant data / stor. 1 tab, and select the Batch Management checkbox.
10. Assign the batch class to the material in the material master by navigating to the
Classification tab, entering class type “023” and the class name (in this example,
“SHELFLIFE_PPDS”) in the Class column, and activating Advanced Planning for the
material.
After these steps are completed, when batches are created in SAP S/4HANA inventory
management with shelf-life data entered, the batches are automatically transferred to
PP/DS with the shelf-life information.
The batches are represented as versions in PP/DS, and the shelf-life details are dis-
played in the Elements tab of the product view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3), as shown
in the upper part of Figure 8.7.
Figure 8.7 Batches with Shelf Life in PP/DS
© 

479
8.1 Planning with Shelf Life
The batches with quantities are displayed in the Elements tab of the product view, and
the shelf-life expiry date is displayed in the Sl Time 2 column. If batches are created
without the shelf-life classification data in SAP S/4HANA, those batches won’t have any
shelf life calculated in the PP/DS.
Note
In SAP S/4HANA, the shelf-life data maintained in the material master Plant data / stor.
1 view is considered for calculating the shelf-life expiry for batches, and the same is
transferred to PP/DS. The location-specific shelf-life data maintained in the Advanced
Planning tab is only considered by PP/DS applications for objects created by PP/DS, such
as planned orders, dependent demands, and so on.
In the Versions tab of the product view, all available batches for the material are dis-
played. As shown on the lower part of Figure 8.7, the green icon on the Cl. Status col-
umn indicates that the batch is classified correctly.

sections.title: Pegging and Planning
sections.text:
8.1.3 Pegging and Planning
While generating the dynamic pegging relationships for materials with shelf-life data,
the system checks for the compatibility of the requirement element and the matura-
tion time, as well as the shelf life of a receipt or stock element. Only compatible ele-
ments will participate in pegging relationships. The batch stocks without the correct
classification for shelf-life data can only be assigned to requirement elements without
any shelf-life requirement conditions.
When a receipt element such as a batch is available in PP/DS, the system considers its
expiry date and the minimum shelf-life requirements to create dynamic pegging. For
example, as shown in Figure 8.8, a forecast demand element is created with a require-
ment date of 08.10.2023, and the system calculates the minimum shelf life required as
18.10.2023 by adding the Min. Shelf Life (10 days) to the requirement date (08.10.2023)
1 and the required maximum shelf life as 07.10.2024 by adding the Max. Shelf Life (365
days) to the requirement date (08.10.2023) 2.
These dates are calculated from the location-specific shelf-life data maintained in the
Advanced Planning view of the material master, as shown in Figure 8.9. Because none
of the available receipts fulfill these shelf-life requirements from the demand ele-
ments, no dynamic pegging is established for this forecast. If there is a receipt element
with a shelf-life expiry date between 18.10.2023 and 07.10.2024, then the forecast ele-
ment will be pegged to that receipt element.

8 Advanced PP/DS Features
480
Figure 8.8 Dynamic Pegging in PP/DS Considering Shelf-Life Data
Figure 8.9 Pegging Considering Shelf Life: No Pegging without Suitable Elements
The planning of standard lots heuristic algorithm (/SAPAPO/HEU_PLAN_STANDARD-
LOTS; see Chapter 5, Section 5.3.1) in PP/DS supports planning of products with shelf-life
requirements. In the standard system, heuristic planning of standard lots with shelf life
(SAP_PP_SL001) is delivered and can be assigned as the product heuristic for the rele-
vant products, as shown in Figure 8.10. The Plan with Shelf Life setting in the Heuristics
Settings screen for Planning of Std Lots with Shelf Life, as shown in Figure 8.10, is
required for the shelf life to be considered during planning using this heuristic.
© 

481
8.1 Planning with Shelf Life
Figure 8.10 Planning Standard Lots with Shelf-Life Heuristic in PP/DS
During net requirement calculation using the SAP_PP_SL001 heuristic, the compatibil-
ity of the receipt elements and requirement with respect to maturation time, mini-
mum/maximum shelf life, and shelf-life expiry dates is considered. If there are fixed
receipts without shelf-life compatibility for any of the requirement elements, excess
receipts will result.
The following rules are applied to check for the compatibility of the stock or receipt ele-
ment and the requirement elements:
 Maturation time
The stock or receipt element must have completed the maturation time by the
requirements date.
 Minimum shelf life
The stock or receipt element must not expire at least before the required minimum
shelf life of the requirements element.
 Maximum shelf life
The stock or receipt element can have an expiry date at most until the required max-
imum shelf life of the requirements element.

sections.title: Alerts for Shelf Life
sections.text:
8.1.4 Alerts for Shelf Life
In the PP/DS Alert Monitor, specific alerts are provided to monitor the shelf life–related
exceptions. There are three main categories of alerts related to shelf life of the receipt
and requirement element: maturation time, shelf-life violations, and expiring receipts.

8 Advanced PP/DS Features
482
Maturation Time
Maturation time is the time after the receipt date, a duration during which the material
can’t be used for consumption as a component to another manufacturing step or to
fulfill demand elements such as sales order or forecast elements. The alerts related to
maturation time can be raised both on the receipt element and the requirement ele-
ment to which the receipt element is pegged.
As shown in Figure 8.11, the alert profile is set to create an alert if the receipt is still in its
maturation period and yet pegged to the requirement element because there are no
other matching receipt elements available for the product/location. In this example, the
alert profile is set to create a red alert if the difference between the requirement element
and the receipt element’s maturation duration is more than 10 hours 1. In the bottom
part of the screen, you’ll see that the receipt element (planned order) 2 will finish its
maturation period on 25.03.2023 3 (receipt date 20.03.2023 + 5 days of location specific
maturity time), but it’s pegged to the requirement element 4 on 22.03.2023. As the dif-
ference between the requirement date and the end of maturity date is more than 10
hours, the alerts 5 are raised for both the receipt element and the requirement element.
Figure 8.11 Maturation Date Alerts in Shelf-Life Planning
Shelf-Life Violations
The shelf-life violation alerts can be raised when the receipt element is expiring before
the minimum shelf-life required for the requirement element, or if the receipt element
expires after the maximum allowed shelf-life for the requirement element.
© 

483
8.1 Planning with Shelf Life
When dynamic pegging is used, these alert types aren’t relevant because with dynamic
pegging the receipt elements will never get pegged to the requirement if the shelf-life
conditions are violated. These alerts can be raised if a fixed pegging exists between the
receipt and requirement element, and the dates of either the receipt or requirement
element have changed after the fixed pegging is created.
In the example shown in Figure 8.12, there is a fixed pegging relationship 1 created
between the planned order 2 on 05.12.2023 (expires on 15.03.2023), and the forecast
requirement element 3 on 22.03.2023 (requires a receipt that doesn’t expire on
01.04.2021 [minimum shelf life required]). As the alert profile is configured to raise a
warning alert if the shelf-life violation is more than one hour 4, an alert is raised for the
receipt and the requirement element 5.
Figure 8.12 Alerts for Shelf-Life Violation in Fixed Pegging
Expiring Receipts with No Consumption of the Receipt
This alert type is one of the important ones. When receipt elements such as batch
stocks, planned orders, and production/process orders have a shelf life assigned to
them, and they can’t be pegged to any requirement elements due to violation of mini-
mum or maximum shelf-life conditions, this alert is raised. The planners need to act
upon this alert to take appropriate actions to delete the receipt element (planned
order), cancel the process/production order, or move the inventory to blocked/quality
inspection for reinspection.
In the alert profile, as shown in Figure 8.13, the thresholds are defined based on the
remaining shelf life of the receipt element. In this example 1, if the remaining shelf life
is less than 15 days (360 hours), an info alert is raised; if the remaining shelf life is less
than 10 days (240 hours), a warning alert is raised; and if the remaining shelf life is less

8 Advanced PP/DS Features
484
than 5 days (120 hours), an error alert is raised. There are supply elements such as the
planned orders and the batch stock 2, which aren’t pegged to any requirement ele-
ment, as they can’t fulfill minimum shelf-life conditions for the requirement element.
Therefore, depending on the leftover shelf life of these elements, the alerts are raised 3.
Figure 8.13 Alerts for Expiring and Unconsumed Receipt Elements

sections.title: Product Interchangeability
sections.text:
8.2 Product Interchangeability
During the life of a product in product lifecycle management, there will be changes
required to the components of the materials due to a supplier stopping a specific com-
ponent; for safety, quality, or product improvement issues; or for a regulatory man-
date. These changes require components or products to be discontinued and
substituted with a successor product or component.
In SAP S/4HANA, the discontinuation of a material and assigning a follow-up material
can be done from the MRP 4 view of the material master. However, this method has
restrictions, such as the inability to create multilevel discontinuations (material B
replaces material A, and then material C replaces material B) and that control for the use
of existing stock for discontinued material may also require updating the discontinua-
tion information in the bill of material (BOM) master data for material requirements
planning (MRP) to consider the discontinuation. But SAP S/4HANA discontinuation
supports certain functionalities such as parallel discontinuation, where a group of com-
ponents can be replaced by another group of components with the discontinuation
group assigned in the BOM master data. This isn’t supported in PP/DS product inter-
changeability.
© 

485
8.2 Product Interchangeability
The interchangeability in PP/DS should only be considered for planning purposes
during the transition period from the discontinued component to the replacement
component. The existence of an interchangeability group won’t eliminate the require-
ment to update the BOM master data, which is used by other areas, such as product
costing, in SAP S/4HANA.
Embedded PP/DS supports the discontinuation and substitution via the product inter-
changeability functionality; detailed scheduling supports the discontinuation via the
linear supersession chain where only one product in the chain is valid at any given
point in time. Procurement planning (both in-house and external procurement) and
order processing are supported in PP/DS interchangeability. You can also use the use-
up strategy in PP/DS product interchangeability to control whether the existing stock
can be used to cover requirements until the stock completely depletes for the discon-
tinued material or whether the discontinuation is in effect without consideration of
the existing stock.
Following are some of the restrictions applicable to PP/DS product interchangeability:
 Embedded PP/DS only supports simple interchangeability (1:1). Configurable prod-
ucts can’t participate in interchangeability.
 For integrating manufacturing orders with product substitutions, the interchangeabil-
ity should not have multiple substitutions within one chain (e.g., product A – B – C).
 If shelf-life planning is in use, all the products in the interchangeability chain should
have the same shelf-life conditions.
Now, let’s go through the relevant master data to see how interchangeability works in
the planning process.

sections.title: Master Data
sections.text:
8.2.1 Master Data
PP/DS product interchangeability works based on the following master data objects,
which we’ll discuss in this section:
 Interchangeability group (supersession chain)
 Assignment of the interchangeability group to the supply chain model
 Automatic generation and assignment of planning packages
Interchangeability Group
You create the interchangeability group of type supersession chain using Transaction
/INCMD/UI or using SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Master
Data  Product and Location Interchangeability  Interchangeability Group.
As shown in Figure 8.14, in the interchangeability transaction, the screen has four main
sections:

8 Advanced PP/DS Features
486
 Quick Search
This can be used for searching the existing interchangeability groups in the system;
the search results are displayed at the bottom of the screen.
 Header
The interchangeability group header has the Group Type (only supersession chain is
supported in PP/DS), Group name, Group Description, and Relevant for fields. In the
SAP S/4HANA system, advanced available-to-promise (aATP) and PP/DS aren’t
directly integrated, so select Planning in the Relevant for field. The Status is set to In
Process when the group is created and saved without releasing the same. You can
use the Release button on the menu bar to set the Status to Released.
Figure 8.14 Interchangeability Group in PP/DS
 Location
In the Location tab, assign the locations for which the interchangeability group is rel-
evant. The materials being maintained in the interchangeability group should be
available in the locations defined in the Location tab of the header data.
 Details
The Details tab of the interchangeability transaction screen contains the details of
the materials that are assigned as the preceding and succeeding materials in the
interchangeability group and the attributes of the interchangeability relationship.
After the header data is entered, navigate to the Location-Independent Attributes sec-
tion under Details, and click on the Append Row button (new document symbol icon)
on the toolbar to add a new row. You can enter the details of the preceding and succeed-
ing materials and the attributes in the row by clicking the number in the Item No. col-
umn and arriving at the Basic Data tab, as shown in Figure 8.15. You also can click the
© 

487
8.2 Product Interchangeability
row in the Attributes tab, and the row will be expanded into a new screen, as shown in
Figure 8.16.
Figure 8.15 Maintenance of Interchangeability Group Details: Basic Data
Figure 8.16 Maintenance of the Interchangeability Group: Attributes
As shown in Figure 8.16, the group details can be maintained at a Cross-Location level or
Location-Specific level in the Location dropdown. The cross-location details maintained
are applicable for all locations assigned to the interchangeability header, and the prod-
ucts participate in interchangeability maintained in the details. If there is a require-
ment to maintain different values for specific plants, then select the location from the
Location dropdown menu, and maintain the details. For example, material A is
replaced by material B in plant 1, 2, and 3 from 01.Jan.2023. However, in plant 2, if the
interchangeability is valid only from 01.Feb.2023, the same can be maintained as a
location-specific Valid-from Date in the attributes.
PP/DS only supports linear supersession chains, which means that the chain can have
only one preceding and succeeding material. Multiple interchangeability (nonlinear

8 Advanced PP/DS Features
488
supersession chain) isn’t supported in PP/DS, where a product has several successor
products (1:N), or several products have one successor product (N:1). The materials par-
ticipating in the supersession chain should follow these prerequisites:
 The materials in the supersession chain have to be different. Material A-B-A isn’t
supported.
 The supersession chain may not contain any assemblies.
 A material can only be contained in one supersession chain. When a material that is
part of another interchangeability group is assigned to a supersession chain, the sys-
tem will raise an error message.
 The base unit of measure must be the same for all materials in a supersession chain.
 A supersession chain may not contain any configurable products.
 The shelf-life data must be the same for all products in a supersession chain.
In the Basic Data tab (refer to Figure 8.15), enter the material to be discontinued in the
Material Number field under Preceding Member Details, and enter the material that
will replace the discontinued material in the Material Number field under Succeeding
Member Details.
In the Attributes tab (refer to Figure 8.16), enter the date in the Valid-from Date from
which the system should consider the interchangeability to switch the requirements of
the discontinued material to the follow-up material. The interchangeability Direction
field has two options:
 Full
The preceding and succeeding materials can interchange each other.
 Forward
The succeeding material will replace the preceding material from the valid-from
date.
The value defined in the Use-up Strategy field is used to determine how the existing
stock for the preceding material is treated. The options are as follows:
 Yes
Use the existing stock first; only when the stock is depleted, switch over the demand
for the preceding material to the succeeding material.
 No
Irrespective of the existing stock for the preceding material, switch over the demand
from the preceding material to the succeeding material on the valid-from date.
 Restricted
With a restricted use-up strategy, a Use-up Date can be defined, and the existing
stock of the preceding material is used up only until the use-up date.
The Succeeding Quantity Factor and Preceding Quantity Factor are used in scenarios
where the replacement quantity factors between the preceding and succeeding material
© 

489
8.2 Product Interchangeability
aren’t equal. For example, material A replaces material B, but two quantities of material
B are required to replace one quantity of material A. In this case, the Preceding Quantity
Factor is defined as 1, and the Succeeding Quantity Factor is defined as 2.
Set the status of the interchangeability group to Released by clicking on the Release
button in the menu bar of the screen, and click the Save button to save the interchange-
ability group data.
Assign the Interchangeability Group to a Model
For a released interchangeability group to be considered for planning, it must be
assigned to the supply chain model. In embedded PP/DS, 000 is the active model. You
can assign the group to the 000 model by executing Transaction /SAPAPO/INCMD_
MODEL or navigating to the transaction via SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics 
Advanced Planning  Master Data  Product and Location Interchangeability  Assign
Interchangeability Group to a Model.
Enter the Interchangeability Group in the initial screen, and click on the Execute but-
ton, as shown in the upper-left screen of Figure 8.17. On the Assignment of interchange-
ability group model popup screen, all the available models defined in the system are
listed. Select Model Name 000, and click on the Assign Objects to Model button (to the
right of the green checkmark) to assign the interchangeability group to the model 000.
Figure 8.17 Assigning the Interchangeability Group to Model 000
Planning Packages
When materials are assigned to supersession chains, these materials must be planned
together. When executing MRP in PP/DS or executing product heuristics, it’s essential
that all the materials in the chain are planned together to avoid any excess supply
being created for the materials. When the interchangeability groups are assigned with

8 Advanced PP/DS Features
490
a location in the interchangeability master data, the system automatically creates a
planning package and assigns it to all the materials in the material master Advanced
Planning view.
Note
Planning packages can also be used in regular planning scenarios if there is a require-
ment to plan certain materials together irrespective of their position in the BOMs (low-
level codes). For interchangeability, a special planning package type 001 is delivered in
the standard system.
For the automatic generation of the planning packages, several Customizing entries
are delivered in standard embedded PP/DS.
The planning package type can be verified from Customizing menu path, SAP IMG
Menu  Advanced Planning  MRP Planning Run  Maintain Planning Package Types. As
shown in Figure 8.18, the Heuristic SAP_PP_I001 is assigned to Package Type 001. This
heuristic calls the product heuristics assigned to the material in the material master for
all the materials in the supersession chain in the correct order, and the product heuris-
tics will decide which requirements are to be passed on to the successor product from
the discontinued product. The heuristics will also consider settings such as the Use-up
Strategy maintained in the interchangeability group master data.
Figure 8.18 Planning Package Type: Customizing
Setting the Automat. Maintenance checkbox in Customizing for the 001 package type
enables the system to generate and update the material master with the planning pack-
age automatically.
In addition, the number range for the automatically generated planning packages must
be maintained via Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  MRP

sections.title: Interchangeability in the Planning Process
sections.text:
8.2.2 Interchangeability in the Planning Process
Materials involved in interchangeability can be planned via MRP runs in the produc-
tion planning run, interactive planning by executing the product heuristics in the plan-
ning tools, or automatic planning triggered by the planning procedure definition. In all
these cases, the system considers the planning package and always executes the super-
session chain heuristic (SAP_PP_I001), which in turn will call the product heuristics
assigned to the material master.

8 Advanced PP/DS Features
492
In the planning package created by the interchangeability group, the sequence of materi-
als is also maintained according to the interchangeable direction (predecessor material
first and successor material next). When MRP is executed for one material in the plan-
ning package, it automatically reads the package and executes planning for all the mate-
rials in the package according to the sequence of materials within the planning package.
In the PP/DS planning run, for the interchangeable products to the planned correctly,
one prerequisite is that the MRP heuristics should have the setting to execute the prod-
uct heuristics in the heuristics customization. In addition, while defining the planning
steps in the production planning run, you must ensure that none of the interchange-
able materials are part of a planning step that executed a procurement planning heu-
ristic (e.g., planning of standard lots [SAP_PP_002]) other than MRP heuristics. By
executing a procurement heuristic other than the MRP heuristics, the planning pack-
age sequence of materials can’t be ensured, and the planning results may be incorrect.
During the planning, the requirement of the predecessor product may need to be cov-
ered by the successor product based on the validity of the supersession chain and the
use-up strategy maintained in the interchangeability group. In this case, the system
will generate an order of type substitution order (Subst.ord) to transfer the demand
from the predecessor (RAW1) to the successor material to cover the DepDmd, as shown
in the Elements tab in Figure 8.20 1. The substitution order will have the predecessor
material as an input (RAW2 under Requirements) and the successor material as an out-
put component (RAW1 under Receipts) in the order 2. The substitution orders can’t be
manually changed, and these are considered unfirmed orders for the purpose of plan-
ning, so that the planning run can adjust them per the demand and supply situation.
A pegging relationship is established between the original requirement element (in
Figure 8.20, the DepDmd) and the substitution order. So, during detailed scheduling
activities, if the strategy profile is set to respect dynamic pegging, then the substitution
orders can also be rescheduled along with the requirement element.
Note
MRP Live (Transaction MD01N) can’t plan products with interchangeability, so a PP/DS
planning run with MRP heuristics must be executed for such materials.
Because the substitution orders aren’t transferred to SAP S/4HANA, the demand and
supply situation in transactions such as the stock requirements list (Transaction
MD04) may state excess supply for the predecessor product and supply deficiency for
the successor product. Therefore, it’s essential that only PP/DS planning tools are used
to monitor and plan these materials.
For in-house production orders with interchangeable components, it’s mandatory that
the planned orders are set with the conversion checkbox in embedded PP/DS so that
the interchangeability is taken into account in the manufacturing order (production
order or process order).

sections.text:
8.3 Characteristics-Dependent Planning
As discussed in Chapter 2, Section 2.6, and Chapter 3, Section 3.2.4, embedded PP/DS
supports variant configuration (VC) or characteristics-dependent planning (CDP). CDP
can also be used in make-to-stock (MTS) scenarios. All the supply and demand ele-
ments, such as forecast elements, planned orders, production orders, and stocks/
batches, have their own classification (assignment of characteristics values), and PP/DS
supports planning that considers these characteristics value assignments. When deter-
mining the net requirement calculation, the system checks the compatibility of the
characteristics values and creates receipts if there are no matching receipt elements
available to fulfill demand elements with specific characteristics values. In addition,
the characteristics value compatibility is considered while creating pegging relation-
ships.
Along with the material master classification, the classification master data—such as
the object dependencies that are created in SAP S/4HANA to control the material and
operation selections in BOMs and routings—can also be sent to the corresponding pro-
duction data structure (PDS) master data in PP/DS.
Note
Conversion from VC to CDP or vice versa can be performed in embedded PP/DS using
ABAP program /SAPAPO/CONFR_CFGREL_MAINTAIN. Caution should be exercised,
however, when doing the conversion after master data and/or transaction data has
already been created in the system because the conversion may lead to inconsistencies
and/or data loss. The report performs a where-used list for finding the materials that
will be impacted; if no inconsistencies are detected, it will complete the conversion.
Adjustment of the materials to reassign the correct classification (classes of the correct
type) must be done manually as a post step. In addition, the transaction data must be
retransferred to PP/DS from SAP S/4HANA.
In the next sections, we’ll cover how PP/DS planning and pegging processes consider
the characteristics and also the steps to set up block planning.

8.3.1 Planning and Pegging
When embedded PP/DS is set with the CDP configuration schema, the system consid-

location to determine the deficit in supply quantity.

assigned with Class Type 300 (variant class). Upon integration (see Chapter 2, Section

tion of the material in PP/DS can be displayed from the PP/DS product master
(Transaction /SAPAPO/MAT1) 3.
Figure 8.22 CDP Classification in SAP S/4HANA and in PP/DS Master Data
Heuristics such as the planning of standard lots can consider the characteristics value

Clicking on the icon shows the characteristics values assigned to the demand element
or the supply element.

sections.title: Block Planning
sections.text:
8.3.2 Block Planning
One of the commonly used features of PP/DS in CDP is block planning. Block planning
is the preassignment of capacities to produce materials belonging to certain character-
istics. This is widely used in mill production (paper, metal, etc.).
In process-oriented manufacturing, when the manufacturing process for a product has
started, it can’t be interrupted or stopped due to the nature of manufacturing pro-
cesses. In such cases, a preassigned capacity for the manufacturing resource is created
via a campaign. This process is called campaign planning. A campaign is created for the
resource in PP/DS, and a group of orders is assigned to the campaign. In addition, the
setup and cleanup orders can be created at the start or end of the production campaign.
The orders in the campaigns can be determined via the setup groups assigned to the
operations of the orders, which in turn results in similar products and their orders
being assigned to the campaign.
In discrete manufacturing, however, materials must be grouped based on the opera-
tion and resource in which the material is being produced. For example, a product may
go through multiple operations, and if there is a bottleneck resource that requires con-
siderable setup for switching the products, the schedule of that work center must be
frozen to preassign its capacity to perform operations with certain characteristics. In
PP/DS, this can be achieved via block planning. In block planning, blocks are created in
the resources with specific characteristics, and operations with the same characteris-
tics values will be scheduled in those blocks.

8 Advanced PP/DS Features
498
For campaign planning in process industries, the campaigns can also be integrated to
SAP S/4HANA. However, in block planning, the blocks are only relevant in PP/DS, and
only the schedule of the operation and the order are integrated back to SAP S/4HANA.
Master Data
The materials for which block planning is to be executed are assigned with class type
300 (variant class), which will generate class type 400 (CDP classification) in embedded
PP/DS. The blocks are created in the resource master data in PP/DS. You create the work
center master data in SAP S/4HANA and activate the Advanced Planning checkbox in
the Basic Data view of the work center master data (see Chapter 2, Section 2.4). This will
integrate the work center into the resource master data on the PP/DS side. When
resources are created in PP/DS, they are assigned to the 000 model and the 000 ver-
sion, which are the active model and version in PP/DS. In addition, model-independent
resource master data is generated.
Maintain Blocks
To create blocks for resources, the first step is to create the basic definition and reference
cycle, which we’ll discuss in this section. You can maintain blocks of the resource master
data in PP/DS using the resource master Transaction /SAPAPO/RES01. The block basis
definition is maintained at the model-independent resource. On the initial screen of the
resource master data, select the Model-Independent Selection checkbox, as shown on the
upper screen of Figure 8.27, and press (Enter). In the next screen, you’ll see the resource
master data that is assigned to the 000 version as well as the model-independent (no ver-
sion assigned) resource data, as shown on the lower screen in Figure 8.27.
Figure 8.27 Model-Independent Resource Master Data

on the Create Blocks button to launch the Maintain Blocks screen (see lower area of
Figure 8.28).
Figure 8.28 Block Planning: Maintain Block Basis Definition
In this screen, navigate to the Block Basis Definit. tab. List the block definitions by

In SAP S/4HANA, object dependencies are defined to select the relevant components

Blocks in Planning and in Scheduling

the same date/time, when the production planning heuristic is creating the receipt

elements as mandated by the strategy profile, the blocks are considered, and orders are
scheduled to place them on the correct blocks (with matching characteristics values).

has changed, and the operations on the impacted blocks need to be rescheduled.
 SAP_CDPBP_02 (adjust and reschedule block limits)
When there are overload or underload situations, the adjust and reschedule block

 SAP_CDPBP_03 (enhanced block maintenance)
This heuristic calls up the block maintenance screen for adjustment (creation,

sections.text:
8.4 Push Production
Figure 8.36 Blocks in the Detailed Scheduling Planning Board and Assignment of Orders to
the Blocks
8.4 Push Production
Push production is the process of creating a production plan to consume excess supply
of a material. Push production is a purely manual process to create a production plan
to consume excess supply of materials with no requirements. The push production
tool helps in making decisions to consume such products.
In a typical production planning scenario, the requirements of the lower-level materi-
als in the BOM levels are determined by the demand of the materials in the higher lev-
els of the BOM structure. Push production works in the opposite way by finding the
higher-level materials that can be produced using the lower-level materials.
In industries such as dairy, food processing, and so on, raw materials are procured
based on long-term contracts, and a slight reduction in the demand for certain finished
products or a production scheduling problem such as machine breakdown to produce
a specific product can result in an oversupply of raw materials. In addition, the shelf life
of such raw materials plays a major role in determining if there is a push problem for a
material. For products with excess coverage, a low shelf life is required to consume the
material or to convert it into another material with a higher shelf life.
In this section, we’ll cover the details on how to identify a push problem in the supply
chain and how the push production tool can help in resolving the same.

8 Advanced PP/DS Features
506

sections.title: Identify the Push Problem
sections.text:
8.4.1 Identify the Push Problem

sections.title: Tank Planning
sections.text:
8.5 Tank Planning
Tank planning is an interactive planning process where raw materials, intermediates,
or finished products need to be stored in tanks, and the tanks have minimum/maxi-
mum storage requirements. Products can be filled into the tank for inbound external
receipts such as purchase requisitions, stock transfer receipts, and receipts from
planned or process orders. The draining from the tanks is represented by consumption
from the tanks by demand elements as dependent demands for in-house manufactur-
ing orders (planned/process orders), sales order demands, and stock transfer demands.
The maintenance of the storage characteristics for the storage resources (tanks) was
already covered in Chapter 2 for master data. In this section, we’ll look into the example
shown in Figure 8.39. Raw material is procured externally and filled into a tank, and the
raw material is drained from the tank for the consumption of producing a finished
product. The finished product is stored/filled in a tank, which has an option of storing
in alternative tanks, and the finished product tank is drained by a stock transfer
demand. We’ll look into the configuration, the master data settings, and the process of
interactive planning using tanks (storage resources).
Figure 8.39 Example of a Tank Planning Scenario
Note
As of SAP S/4HANA release 2022, the tank planning process is supported for interactive
planning, where the tank fill levels can be visualized in the planning tools, manual
rescheduling is required to resolve fill level violations, and alerts can be set up for viola-
tions. Future road map items for embedded PP/DS includes consideration of tank con-
straints in automatic planning and scheduling including Production Planning Optimizer
and Detailed Scheduler Optimizer engines.

sections.title: Configuration
sections.text:
8.5.1 Configuration
There are two main Customizing settings required to set up the tank planning scenario
in PP/DS. The product storage definition (PSD) configuration defines default values
and settings for the creation of the PSDs, and the visualization settings enable the
graphical visualization of the stock levels in the storage resources in tools such as the
detailed scheduling planning board. We’ll cover the details of these customizations
next.
Product Storage Definitions
Apart from setting up the storage characteristics such as the min/max stock levels and
the threshold for setting the fill levels to 0, another master data object called product
storage definition (PSD) is required. The storage definitions can be automatically gener-
ated when integrating the master recipes from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS. For
setting the default values and activation of PSD creation, navigate to SAP IMG menu
path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Tank Planning with Container Resources  Maintain
Settings for Tank Planning with Container Resources. In this Customizing transaction,
there are two main screen areas, as shown in Figure 8.40.
Figure 8.40 Configuration of Default Values for Product Storage Definitions
Under the Defaults for PSD for Inhouse Production (Source Type PDS) area of the config-
uration, you can configure the default values for the PSDs for the product data struc-
tures (PDSs). When the master recipes are integrated to PP/DS via Transaction
CURTOADV_CREATE, based on the settings maintained here, the default values are set
in the PSDs.
Consumption Type for Draining Activities refers to how the draining from the tank is
defined. The following options are available:

8 Advanced PP/DS Features
510
 Start of Activity
The draining is defined as an operation in the master recipe, and the tank from
which the material to be drained is assigned to the operation/phase. A duration will
be assigned in the draining step phase. With the Start of Activity setting, the draining
is performed at the start time stamp of the activity of the planned/process order.
 End of Activity
The draining of the tank that stores the material is performed at the time stamp of
the end of the activity.
 Continual Consumption
In scenarios where the draining is continuous, this setting can be used. For example,
if 1,000 liters of liquid needs to be consumed from the storage tank to the processing
unit over a duration of 10 hours, every 1 hour, 100 liters of liquid are drained from
the tank into the processing unit.
 Undefined
No default value is set during the automatic creation of the PSD during PDS integra-
tion, and the consumption type needs to be manually maintained in the product
PSD master data.
Similarly, for the filling of the tanks, the default value for the way the tanks are filled is
set in the Consumption Type for Filling Activities.
Select the Generate Product Storage Definition During PDS Generation checkbox to
automatically generate the PSD during PDS integration of master recipes.
Note
You can automate the PSD generation during PDS integration using business add-in
(BAdI) /SAPAPO/CURTO_CREATE method CREATE_STORAGE_DEF. If this BAdI is implemented,

sections.text:
8.6 Production Campaign Planning
Figure 8.53 Alerts for Container Resources
8.6 Production Campaign Planning
Production campaign planning is a process of grouping orders with similar characteris-
tics to be produced on the same bottleneck production line. For example, if a manufac-
turing line manufactures various colors of paints, it makes sense to keep the same-
colored paint orders together before switching to another color. In such production
lines, to switch between products with different characteristics, there is a setup or clea-
nout time involved. So, in the production campaign planning processes in PP/DS,
objects called production campaigns are created, and orders with the same setup group
are assigned to the campaigns.
Apart from the setup and cleanout times and the associated costs, the storage of the
products may also incur costs. For example, if an intermediate material is produced
and stored in a container that incurs high costs to maintain the container when prod-
ucts are stored, it needs to be consumed by the subsequent production of the finished
product to keep the storage cost minimal. In PP/DS production campaign planning,
there are various tools available to create and manage such campaigns:
 Transaction /SAPAPO/PCMT (Production Campaign)
This transaction is available in the PP/DS system to manually create and manage the
production campaigns in a tabular form.

8 Advanced PP/DS Features
522
 Detailed scheduling planning board
This allows you to graphically visualize the production campaigns and leverage dedi-
cated heuristics that are available for creating and managing production campaigns.
 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer
Detailed Scheduling Optimizer is used to evaluate the setup matrix to reduce the
setup times and costs, as well as optimize the storage costs associated with changes
in the sequencing of the orders. Detailed Scheduling Optimizer optimizes the setup
times/costs and storage costs, and it also creates the production campaigns.
The production campaigns are also objects in the SAP S/4HANA system. So, the embed-
ded PP/DS campaigns are also integrated via the core interface to SAP S/4HANA. In the
SAP S/4HANA side, there are processes to handle the campaigns with respect to prod-
uct costing.
The functionality of block planning isn’t to be confused with campaign planning. Block
planning focuses on predefining blocks at the resource level of certain durations with
preassigned characteristics for the block, so that the orders with characteristics can
only be scheduled in those blocks. The blocks are PP/DS master data objects and have
no relevance in SAP S/4HANA.
Next, we’ll cover the required configuration settings, master data objects, and various
tools that can be leveraged in PP/DS to perform the production campaign planning.

sections.title: Configuration
sections.text:
8.6.1 Configuration
The configuration settings required for campaign planning consists of setting up the
number ranges for the campaigns in PP/DS, the campaign profiles that define the color
of the campaigns, and the visualization settings to graphically represent the campaigns
in the detailed scheduling planning board.
Number Ranges
The production campaigns created in PP/DS are assigned with PP/DS campaign num-
bers. When they are integrated to SAP S/4HANA, the campaigns will get assigned an
external campaign number (i.e., the campaign number assigned in SAP S/4HANA). But
the PP/DS campaign number is retained throughout the campaign’s lifecycle.
Figure 8.54 Number Range Assignment for PP/DS Production Campaigns
© 

523
8.6 Production Campaign Planning
To manage the number range of the PP/DS production campaigns, navigate to SAP IMG
menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Global Settings  Maintain Number Ranges for
Production Campaigns. In this transaction, if no default entry is available, create a new
number range for the default object PCM. You can also change the existing number
range assignments from this transaction, as shown in Figure 8.54.
Campaign Profile
The campaign profile is an object used by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer when creat-
ing optimized campaigns. To create the campaign profile, navigate to SAP IMG menu
path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Production Campaign Planning  Maintain Campaign
Profile. The campaign profile is based on the setup groups that are assigned to the master
recipe operations. The characteristics-based generated setup groups aren’t available for
selection while creating the campaign profile. So, these setup groups should exist in the
SAP S/4HANA side and are integrated over to embedded PP/DS via an integration model.
The initial screen of this configuration transaction, as shown in Figure 8.55, has a client-
wide setting 1 for the placement of the setup clean-out order. For example, if the cam-
paign is created for orders with a setup group for color white and transitioning to
another campaign for orders for color black, this setting will determine if a cleanout
time needs to be planned at the end of the white color orders’ campaign or a setup time
needs to be planned in the black colored orders’ campaign.
Figure 8.55 Campaign Profile in PP/DS

8 Advanced PP/DS Features
524
To create a new campaign profile, click on the New Entries button 2. In the New Entries
screen, enter a name and description for the campaign profile. Enter the plant in which
the profile is relevant in the Location field. In the Setup Group field, select the setup
group for which this campaign profile is relevant.
Only the static setup groups, which are core interfaced over from SAP S/4HANA, are
available for selection in this field. In the Max. no. of charges field, enter the maximum
number of orders that the optimizer can cover under one campaign. For example, if
there are 50 orders in the optimization horizon with the same setup group, and if the
maximum number of charges is 25, the optimizer would create 2 campaigns with 25
orders each. The Campaign Color field determines the graphical representation of the
campaigns in the detailed scheduling planning board.
Visualization
When campaign planning is leveraged, it’s required to display the campaigns as graph-
ical objects to enable production schedulers to manage the campaigns to add orders,
remove orders, or split the campaigns in the detailed scheduling planning board.
To make the campaign object to be displayed an overarching graphical object covering
the orders contained in the campaign, the detailed scheduling planning board profile
needs to be enabled to display the campaigns. The detailed scheduling planning board
profile can be configured from SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning 
Detailed Scheduling  Settings for the Detailed Scheduling Planning Board  Maintain
Planning Board Profiles. In the standard system, a detailed scheduling planning board
profile SAP_PCM is delivered that has the specific setting in the resource chart settings,
as shown in Figure 8.56.
If you want to combine other requirements for the resource chart along with the cam-
paign planning requirements, enable the Campaigns checkbox in your specific plan-
ning board profile.
The color of the campaign bar in the detailed scheduling planning board is determined
from the campaign profile, when the campaigns are created by a campaign heuristic, or
from the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer. When you create the campaigns manually
from the detailed scheduling planning board, you can select the color of the campaign
for the display in the planning board.
Assign the planning board profile to an overall profile. In the standard system, an over-
all profile “SAP_PCM” is delivered with the required settings for campaign planning in
the detailed scheduling planning board.

8.6.2 Master Data
For campaign planning, especially for the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer to create opti-
mized campaigns, there are specific master data requirements. The storage cost of the
products is defined in the material master, which will be evaluated by the Detailed Sched-
uling Optimizer during campaign optimization to calculate the storage costs if the out-
put of the product isn’t consumed immediately. As shown in Figure 8.57, in the material
master under the Advanced Planning view, maintain the storage cost in the Prod. Storage
Cost field. This cost is to store the material in its base unit of measure for one day.
Figure 8.57 Storage Cost for Products in the Material Master

526
For leveraging the campaign planning functionalities, the resource master should be
activated for campaign planning. As shown in Figure 8.58, in the resource master data
under the capacity header, navigate to the Header Data for APO Resource view, and
select the Campaign Relevant 1 checkbox. When this is activated, during scheduling,
the system will ensure that when campaigns are available on the resource, no new
orders that can’t belong to the campaign (having a different setup group) are scheduled

To create the setup groups, follow SAP IMG menu path, SPRO  Production Planning for
Process Industries  Master Data  Master Recipe  Data for Operations and Phases 
Define Setup Groups and Setup Group Categories. In this example shown in Figure 8.59,

© 

527

Create an integration model for the setup groups using Transaction CFM1, and activate

During the campaign planning process, the system evaluates the setup group assigned

same setup group. To have the setup groups in the PDS, the setup phases in the master
recipe should be assigned with the setup groups, as shown in Figure 8.60. The phase

have a finish-start relationship, and the resource in PP/DS should also be assigned with
the setup matrix for the correct integration of the setup activity to the PP/DS PDS.

PDS
To define the setup matrix in PP/DS, use Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSC7 or follow SAP
Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Master Data  Setup Group/
Setup Matrix. In this simple example, the setup matrix is defined to changeover from
BLACK to WHITE and WHITE to BLACK (see Figure 8.61 1). In campaign planning, when
campaigns are created, there is an option to create setup and cleanout orders, which
will replace the setup activity of the first order in the campaign. These setup/cleanout

528
orders are also integrated to SAP S/4HANA so that the cost of the setup or cleanout can
be distributed to the orders within the same campaign.
When defining the setup matrix, you can assign a PDS to the changeovers so that the

ristics or Detailed Scheduling Optimizer to create the setup/cleanout orders, which will

based on the PDS assigned in the setup matrix. In our example, dummy material S4PP_
DS_SETUP_CLEANOUT is created, and a produce operation is defined with the equal dura-
tion of the changeover transition in its master recipe/PDS. In this example, WHITE to
BLACK and BLACK to WHITE has 5 hours of changeover duration, so only one PDS is gen-
erated with 5 hours (18,000 sec) of produce time 3. It’s important to create these setup/

8.6.3 Campaign Planning Tools
There are various tools in PP/DS that can be used to create and manage the production
campaigns. We’ll cover the details of those tools in this section.
© 

529
8.6 Production Campaign Planning
Production Campaign Transaction
The production campaign transaction is a completely manual process to create produc-
tion campaigns and assign orders to them. No graphical support is available within the
transaction, but the campaigns created in the campaign transactions can be visualized
in the detailed scheduling planning board.
To launch the campaign transaction, follow Sap Easy Access menu path Logistics 
Advanced Planning  Production Planning  Interactive Production Planning  Production
Campaign. You can also use Transaction /SAPAPO/PCMT.
In the initial screen of the transaction shown in Figure 8.62, you can enter the selection
criteria for the existing campaigns and click on the Change or Display 1 button to manage
existing campaigns. To create a new campaign, click on the New Campaign button 2.
Figure 8.62 Campaign Transaction: Selection Screen
In the next screen, shown in Figure 8.63, you’ll see a list of existing campaigns per the
selection options entered in the initial screen. Even with the Create Campaigns option,
the existing campaigns per the selection are displayed in the left side of the screen 1.
To create a new campaign, enter a description and select a color for the campaign. The
color is used for the display of the campaign bar in the detailed scheduling planning
board. To create new planned orders and assign them to the campaign being created,
click on the Create and Add Orders button 2 at the bottom of the screen. This will open
the Create and Add Orders to Production Campaign popup screen. Enter the product,
location, quantity, and dates for the new planned orders, and click on the Create and
Add Orders button 3. The orders will be added to the campaign, but you’ll have to close
4 the popup window to see the added orders. If you want to add existing orders to the
new campaign, you can use the Add Existing Orders button 5.

8 Advanced PP/DS Features
530
Figure 8.63 Manual Creation of Production Campaigns
Once the new campaign is saved, you can see the Ext. Camp. No. field (see Figure 8.64)
1 is updated with the corresponding SAP S/4HANA campaign number. In addition, you
can load the resource in the detailed scheduling planning board with a campaign-rele-
vant overall profile (SAP_PCM is the standard delivered overall profile), and you can
visualize the new campaign 2 in the detailed scheduling planning board.
Figure 8.64 Update of SAP S/4HANA Campaign Number and Campaign Visualization in the
Detailed Scheduling Planning Board
© 

531
8.6 Production Campaign Planning
As this campaign is created manually and doesn’t use the Detailed Scheduling Opti-
mizer, you can see that the finite resource is overloaded with multiple orders in parallel
within the campaign 3.
Heuristics for Campaign Planning
In the standard PP/DS system, there are various heuristics delivered to create and man-
age the production campaigns. We’ll cover the details of these heuristics next. All the
campaign heuristics can be executed interactively in the detailed scheduling planning
board or in the background using the PP/DS planning run (Transaction /SAPAPO/
CDPSB0).
 Create production campaigns
This heuristic with name SAP_PCM_CRT and algorithm /SAPAPO/HEUR_PCM_CRE-
ATE creates new production campaigns based on the existing sequence of the
orders. When there are orders that aren’t sequenced correctly—that is, when orders
with different setup groups are sequenced without considering the reduction in
setup time—the campaigns will be created for every setup group transition. As
shown in Figure 8.65, based on the existing sequence, this heuristic creates cam-
paigns for every setup group transition. In this example, the setup groups are BLACK
and WHITE. The campaign colors green 1 and orange 2 are assigned for these setup
groups, and the campaigns are created accordingly. This heuristic can result in over-
loads 3 on resources if there are existing overloads before execution of this heuris-
tic. So, it’s essential that the resource is scheduled finitely using a heuristic or the
orders are scheduled finitely and optimized for setup times using Detailed Schedul-
ing Optimizer before this heuristic is executed. You can interactively drag and drop
orders between the campaigns, and the campaign dates will be adjusted accordingly.
In addition, you can see that the setup times are still attached to the orders in which
the setup time is attached 4 (no standalone setup/cleanout orders are created). This
heuristic can also be executed in a background planning run (Transaction /SAPAPO/
CDPSB0).
Figure 8.65 Result of the Create Production Campaign Heuristic

8 Advanced PP/DS Features

 Dissolve production campaigns
This heuristic delivered with the name SAP_PCM_DIS and the algorithm /SAPAPO/
HEUR_PCM_DISSOLVE dissolves (deletes) the existing production campaigns on the

This heuristic (SAP_PCM_SRVA) with algorithm /SAPAPO/HEUR_PCM_SERVICE_

paign, the sequence-dependent (based on the setup matrix) setup time of the first
order in the campaign will be replaced with a new planned order using the PDS
assigned in the setup matrix. Whether the system should create a setup order (the
first order within the production campaign), or it should create a cleanout order as
the last order of the preceding campaign (still replacing the sequence dependent

This heuristic (SAP_PCM_ODEL) with algorithm /SAPAPO/HEUR_PCM_ORDERS_
DELETE can be used to delete the setup/cleanout orders in the production campaign.
This heuristic works based on the selection of the product/location. So, in the
detailed scheduling planning board, you need to select the product and execute this
heuristic. As this heuristic will delete all orders, it’s important that you select the
dummy material with which the setup/cleanout orders are created for the cam-

costs without leveraging the campaign optimization in Detailed Scheduling Opti-
mizer, it’s required to delete the setup/cleanout orders before the execution of this
heuristic, so that the setup activities are available in the corresponding planned
orders, which Detailed Scheduling Optimizer can evaluate and optimize.

8.7 Segmentation
Existing Campaigns option determines how existing campaigns are treated during
optimization:
 Dissolve
Dissolve existing campaigns at the start of the optimization, so that new campaigns
are created.
 Extend
Existing campaigns can be added with new orders, and/or the campaigns may be
moved on the same resource in which they were originally created.
 Retain
The existing campaigns can only be moved in the same resource in which they were
originally created. Orders can’t be added or removed from the campaign.
At the end of the optimization, the campaigns are created with an optimized sequence
of orders, so that the setup costs/times are reduced, and a balance between the setup/
storage/delay is achieved. Compared to Figure 8.65, shown earlier, in which the cam-
paign was created using the heuristics, the optimizer-created campaigns, as shown in
Figure 8.70, are finitely scheduled and optimized for changeovers 1. In addition, you
can see that the setup orders 2 are created (replacing the setup activity of the first
order in the campaign), which is also done by the optimizer.
Figure 8.70 Result of Campaign Optimization in the Detailed Scheduling Planning Board
The optimizer and heuristics can be either interactively used or scheduled as a back-
ground job. Irrespective of the PP/DS tool used for creating and managing the cam-
paigns, once the results are saved in PP/DS, they are transferred back to SAP S/4HANA,
and PP/DS is updated with the external campaign number from the SAP S/4HANA sys-
tem.
8.7 Segmentation
Segmentation was originally developed for the fashion industry to segregate the sup-
ply and demand elements for products. The segmentation could be based on different
markets, customers, and so on. For example, if the same product with the same form,
fit, and function is being sold to different markets with different regulatory require-

8 Advanced PP/DS Features
536
ments (e.g., a different statutory label on the product), then, in the SAP systems, sepa-
rate material masters and corresponding BOMs/routings or master recipes are created
for those separate materials. With segmentation in SAP S/4HANA, the demand and
supply elements for the same product can be tagged with a segment value, which helps
avoid the need to create separate master data elements. As similar solution require-
ments are also relevant for other industries, such as life sciences, the segmentation
solution in SAP S/4HANA was enhanced to support non-fashion industry–related mas-
ter and transaction data objects as well.
From SAP S/4HANA 2021, the SAP S/4HANA segmentation solution was improved to
include the segmentation fields in many of the production planning data elements
such as planned orders, process orders, and master recipes. Before SAP S/4HANA 2021,
segmentation was supported in objects such as BOMs, routings, and production orders.
Starting with the SAP S/4HANA 2022 release, the SAP S/4HANA segmentation is also
integrated with embedded PP/DS for enabling segment-dependent planning in PP/DS.
The segmentation supports using CDP as well (refer to Section 8.3 for the details on
CDP).
In this section, we’ll focus on an example of setting up basic data in SAP S/4HANA to
create a segmentation strategy and integrate the CDP data to PP/DS, and illustrate
examples of how master data and transaction data are integrated to PP/DS while
respecting the segmentation data from SAP S/4HANA. We won’t cover the configura-
tion and in-depth details of the segmentation functionality in the SAP S/4HANA side.
Within PP/DS, because CDP is used for segmentation, the configuration schema of the
embedded PP/DS system must be set as CDP.

8.8 Summary
Embedded PP/DS offers many advanced features, including some of the industry-
specific functionalities (e.g., tank planning) covered in this chapter. Other industry-
specific advanced features are also available in the PP/DS system that can be used
across industries, although some of them have an industry flavor.
Following are some of the other advanced PP/DS industry-specific features:
 PP/DS repetitive manufacturing is used by automotive and automotive parts man-
ufacturers or any industry with takt-based scheduling requirements where the prod-
ucts pass through the production line with a predefined time duration at every
assembly or workstation, and components are consumed at the backflushing points.
 PP/DS length-based planning/multiple output planning is used in the mill industry
(e.g., paper, steel, etc.) where the planning is dependent on the length requirement of
the output product from a long raw material.
We’ve covered the setup and working of the planning and scheduling features and also
some of the advanced features offered by embedded PP/DS so far.
In the next chapter, we’ll discuss some of the operations and administration tasks
required to ensure the efficient use of embedded PP/DS.
